correctness.rationale: For any k distinct nonroot labels forced to be root-adjacent leaves, deleting them bijects the event onto the (n-k-1)! remaining uniform recursive trees. Thus E[(Q)_k z^L]=z^k E[z^(L_(n-k))] for k<=n-2, separately z^(n-1) for k=n-1. Eulerian leaf PGF and u^Q factorial expansion give all coefficients and handle n=2. First and mixed derivatives give EQ=1, EQL=(n+1)/2, VarQ=1, VarL=n/12, hence stated covariance and correlation n>=3. The Eulerian-descent bounded 1-dependent CLT and dominated factorial series (summable 1/k! at 0<=u<=1) yield independent joint Poisson-normal limits. Independently enumerated every (n-1)! parent assignment for n=3..7 and checked Cov(Q,L)=1/2 using exact fractions, without treating finite checks as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The local-versus-global leaf statistics measure distinct natural scales of terminal branching. The exact coupled law, finite nonzero covariance and asymptotically independent normalized fluctuations quantify dependence not reconstructible from their separately classical Eulerian and Poisson marginals. It is an all-order exact distribution, not a tiny-instance recomputation.

final_claim: For every n>=2 uniform recursive tree the entire bivariate law E[u^(root leaf-children) z^(total leaves)] equals the Eulerian binomial factorial transform including its exceptional star term; for n>=3 covariance=1/2, correlation=sqrt(3/n), and scaled joint limit is independent Poisson(1) x N(0,1).
limitations: Uniform independent-parent recursive trees only, not preferential attachment or plane increasing trees.
n=2 is deterministic; covariance/correlation statements start at n=3.
Finite brute force n<=7 verifies examples only; independence limit depends on the 1-dependent CLT.
